scenario: A switch port connected to a server shows late collisions and many runts on the switch side. The server is set to full duplex. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The switch port is set to half duplex
The cable exceeds the 300-meter copper limit
options.note: Copper Ethernet is limited to 100 m; but late collisions point to duplex.

options.text: The port is assigned to the wrong VLAN
The server's IP address is wrong

explanation: With a duplex mismatch, the half-duplex side sees late collisions, and the full-duplex side often sees CRC errors and runts. Set both sides to auto or configure them identically.

scenario: Two switches connect with a standard straight-through cable and the link comes up. Which feature makes this work?
explanation: Auto-MDIX detects the cable type and adjusts transmit and receive pairs, so straight-through or crossover cables both work.

scenario: Interface output shows input errors and a rising CRC count, but no collisions. The link is full duplex. What should be checked first?

options.text: The OSPF area number on the uplink
The DHCP pool and lease settings
The VTY line passwords and timeouts

explanation: CRC errors on a full-duplex link usually mean physical problems: damaged cabling, bad terminations, EMI or a failing port or transceiver.

scenario: Which copper Ethernet standard and maximum distance apply to 1000BASE-T?
explanation: 1000BASE-T uses all four pairs of Cat5e (or better) up to 100 meters.

scenario: A switch port shows "down/down" with a fiber transceiver installed. The far end uses multimode fiber at 850 nm. The local SFP is a 1310 nm single-mode module. What is the problem?

options.text: Spanning tree is blocking the port as a loop
The port is in the wrong VLAN

explanation: Both ends must use compatible optics (wavelength and fiber mode). Mismatched transceivers cause no link or a high error rate.

scenario: What does an interface status of "up/down" usually indicate?

options.text: Layer 1 is up, but the data link protocol isn't
The interface is administratively shut down
No cable is connected to the port at all

explanation: The first status is the physical layer and the second is the line protocol. "up/down" points to layer 2 issues such as encapsulation mismatches.

scenario: Which hypervisor type runs directly on the server hardware without a host operating system?

options.note: Runs on top of an OS.

options.text: A container engine on a host OS
options.note: Containers share the host OS kernel.

explanation: Type 1 hypervisors (such as ESXi or Hyper-V Server) are used in data centers. Type 2 hypervisors (such as VirtualBox) run as applications on a desktop OS.

scenario: What is a key difference between containers and virtual machines?

options.text: Containers share the host OS kernel; VMs each run a full guest OS
Containers each include their own full OS kernel and drivers
Containers can only run on type 2 hypervisors

explanation: Containers are lightweight and start quickly because they share the host kernel. VMs provide stronger isolation with their own OS.

scenario: Virtual machines on a host need to communicate with each other and with the physical network. Which component switches their traffic?

options.note: VM traffic on the same host is switched in software.

explanation: Hypervisors include virtual switches that connect VM virtual NICs to each other and to physical uplinks, and can apply VLAN tags.

scenario: A host is configured as 172.16.10.130/25. What are its network and broadcast addresses?
explanation: A /25 splits the last octet into 0–127 and 128–255. Address .130 is in the 128 block.

scenario: Which subnet mask provides at least 500 usable host addresses with the least waste?
explanation: A /23 gives 2⁹ − 2 = 510 usable addresses.

scenario: A router interface needs an address on a point-to-point link with only two hosts. Which prefix is most efficient?
explanation: A /30 provides exactly two usable addresses. Many networks also use /31 on point-to-point links (RFC 3021).

scenario: PC1 is 10.1.1.10/24 with gateway 10.1.2.1. It can ping hosts on 10.1.1.0/24 but not remote networks. What is wrong?

options.text: The default gateway isn't in the PC's subnet
The subnet mask is too large
The PC needs a public IP address to route
options.note: Private addressing is fine with NAT.

options.text: The DNS server address is misconfigured
options.note: Pings by IP would still work.

explanation: The default gateway must be an address in the host's own subnet, normally the router's interface on that segment.

scenario: Which addresses are private IPv4 ranges defined by RFC 1918?
explanation: RFC 1918 private ranges aren't routed on the internet; NAT translates them to public addresses.

scenario: Which wildcard mask matches all hosts in 192.168.40.0/22?
explanation: The wildcard mask is the inverse of the subnet mask: 255.255.255.255 − 255.255.252.0 = 0.0.3.255.

scenario: A router interface with MAC address 0011.2233.4455 uses EUI-64 to build its IPv6 interface ID. What is the interface ID?
explanation: Modified EUI-64 splits the MAC in half, inserts FFFE, and flips the 7th bit of the first byte (00 becomes 02).

scenario: Which IPv6 address type is equivalent to public IPv4 addresses and is routable on the internet?
explanation: Global unicast addresses are globally routable. Unique local addresses are for private use.

scenario: Which command enables a Cisco router to forward IPv6 packets between interfaces?

options.note: Creates a link-local address on an interface.

explanation: Routers need ipv6 unicast-routing to route IPv6 and to send router advertisements.

scenario: Which IPv6 multicast address reaches all nodes on the local link?
explanation: FF02::1 is all nodes and FF02::2 is all routers. Solicited-node multicast (FF02::1:FFxx:xxxx) replaces ARP broadcasts.

scenario: An IPv6 interface is configured with ipv6 address 2001:db8:10::/64 eui-64. How is the full address formed?

options.text: The /64 prefix plus an ID derived from the MAC
The prefix followed by an all-zeros interface ID
options.note: That would be the subnet-router anycast address.

options.text: An address leased from a DHCPv6 server

explanation: The router combines the configured /64 prefix with the modified EUI-64 interface ID.

scenario: Which IPv6 address prefix is used for unique local addresses, similar to private IPv4 addresses?
explanation: Unique local addresses aren't routed on the internet. In practice they use FD00::/8 with a random global ID.

scenario: An office has dense Wi-Fi coverage in the 2.4 GHz band. Which channels should neighboring APs use to avoid overlap?

options.text: Any channels, since they don't overlap in 2.4 GHz

explanation: In the 2.4 GHz band, only channels 1, 6 and 11 don't overlap (in North America).

scenario: Compared with 2.4 GHz, what is a characteristic of the 5 GHz band?

options.text: More non-overlapping channels but shorter range
More interference from microwave ovens and Bluetooth

explanation: Higher frequencies offer more channels and less congestion but attenuate more through obstacles.

scenario: Which wireless security protocol replaces the pre-shared key handshake with SAE?

options.note: Uses PSK with the four-way handshake.

explanation: WPA3-Personal uses Simultaneous Authentication of Equals, which resists offline dictionary attacks.

scenario: A wireless client's signal is strong, but the noise floor is high and throughput is poor. Which metric best describes the problem?

options.text: RSSI that's too high for the client
options.note: A strong signal alone isn't the issue.

options.text: The SSID is mapped to the wrong VLAN

explanation: SNR is the difference between signal strength and noise. Low SNR causes retransmissions and lower data rates.

scenario: Which device commonly causes interference in the 2.4 GHz band?
explanation: Microwave ovens, Bluetooth devices, cordless phones and some cameras use or leak into 2.4 GHz.

scenario: Employees should authenticate to Wi-Fi with their own credentials via a RADIUS server. Which mode should be used?
explanation: Enterprise mode authenticates each user with 802.1X/EAP against a RADIUS server.

scenario: On a Linux host, which command shows the IP addresses assigned to interfaces?
explanation: On Linux, ip addr (or ip a) shows addresses and ip route shows the routing table. macOS uses ifconfig, and Windows uses ipconfig.

scenario: A Windows client shows 169.254.10.20 as its IP address. What does this indicate?

options.text: The client didn't receive a DHCP address
The client has a valid public address
The client is configured for IPv6 only
The client's DNS server is down

explanation: APIPA addresses mean DHCP failed. Check the DHCP server, the DHCP relay and the switch port VLAN.

scenario: A user can ping 8.8.8.8 but can't open websites by name. Which command helps test DNS resolution on Windows?
explanation: nslookup queries DNS servers directly to see whether names resolve and which server answers.

scenario: A laptop connects to the correct SSID but gets an "authentication failed" error, while other users are fine. What should be checked first?

options.text: The client's security settings and credentials
The OSPF configuration on the core router
The switch's STP root bridge priority
The DNS MX records for the domain

explanation: If others connect, check the client's security type (WPA2 vs WPA3, Personal vs Enterprise), password or certificate, and saved profile.

scenario: On macOS, which command displays network interface configuration from the terminal?
explanation: macOS uses ifconfig (and networksetup), and Linux uses ip addr.

scenario: Which IOS command makes a router forward client DHCP broadcasts to a DHCP server at 10.10.10.5?

options.note: A static route doesn't relay DHCP.

explanation: ip helper-address configures the interface as a DHCP relay agent, forwarding broadcasts as unicast to the server.

scenario: Which commands configure a router as a DHCP server for 192.168.1.0/24 with gateway 192.168.1.1?

options.text: ip dhcp pool LAN / network 192.168.1.0 255.255.255.0 / default-router 192.168.1.1

options.note: Configures a relay, not a server.
Makes the interface a DHCP client.

explanation: An IOS DHCP pool defines the network, default-router, dns-server and lease. Use ip dhcp excluded-address to reserve static addresses.

scenario: Which command prevents an IOS DHCP server from handing out 192.168.1.1 through 192.168.1.10?

options.note: Network statements need a network address.

explanation: Excluded addresses are configured in global configuration mode, outside the pool.

scenario: Which command shows the IP addresses an IOS DHCP server has leased to clients?

options.note: Shows a DHCP client's own lease, not server bindings.

explanation: show ip dhcp binding lists leased addresses with client hardware addresses and lease expiration.

scenario: A router interface should obtain its address from the ISP's DHCP server. Which command is used on the interface?
explanation: ip address dhcp makes the router interface a DHCP client.

scenario: Clients on VLAN 30 aren't getting DHCP addresses. The SVI for VLAN 30 has no helper address, and the DHCP server is on VLAN 99. What is the fix?

options.text: Add ip helper-address <server IP> to interface Vlan30
Add ip helper-address <server IP> to interface Vlan99
options.note: It must be on the client-facing interface.

options.text: Enable PortFast on the DHCP server's port
Change the VTP mode to transparent

explanation: The relay must be configured on the interface that receives the client broadcasts, which is the client VLAN's gateway interface.

scenario: Which DHCP message does a client send to accept an offered address?

options.note: Sent by the server to confirm.

explanation: The DORA process: Discover (client), Offer (server), Request (client), Acknowledge (server).

scenario: Which statement about an IPv4 /31 on a point-to-point link is correct?

options.text: Both addresses are usable as host addresses
It still requires a dedicated broadcast address

explanation: On point-to-point links, a /31 saves addresses by using both addresses for the two endpoints.

scenario: What is the purpose of the loopback interface commonly configured on routers?

options.text: A stable, always-up address for management
To provide the physical connection to the ISP
To supply PoE to connected devices
To act as a DHCP relay for every VLAN

explanation: Loopback interfaces never go down unless shut, so they're ideal for OSPF router IDs, management and BGP peering.

scenario: A host sends to 10.2.0.50 from 10.1.0.25/16. How does the host decide whether to use the default gateway?

options.text: It compares the destination with its own subnet
It always sends all traffic to the gateway
It asks the DNS server whether the host is local
options.note: DNS resolves names, not routing decisions.

options.text: It broadcasts an ARP request for the remote host
options.note: Not how forwarding decisions are made.

explanation: 10.1.0.0/16 and 10.2.0.0/16 are different networks, so the host ARPs for its default gateway and sends the packet there.

scenario: Which commands make a switch port an 802.1Q trunk that carries only VLANs 10 and 20?

options.text: switchport mode trunk / switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20
switchport mode access / switchport access vlan 10,20
options.note: Access ports carry one data VLAN.

options.text: switchport mode trunk / switchport trunk native vlan 10,20
options.note: Native VLAN takes one VLAN ID.

explanation: The allowed VLAN list restricts which VLANs cross the trunk. On some platforms, switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q is required first.

scenario: CDP logs "%CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH" on a trunk. What is the problem?

options.text: The two ends of the trunk use different native VLANs
The trunk allows too many VLANs to pass
The trunk port has PortFast enabled
The trunk's interface MTU is set too high

explanation: The native VLAN must match on both ends; otherwise untagged traffic leaks between VLANs.

scenario: Which command assigns an access port to VLAN 30?
explanation: Use switchport mode access and switchport access vlan 30. The VLAN is created automatically if it doesn't exist (on most platforms).

scenario: An IP phone and a PC share a port. The phone's traffic should use VLAN 50 and the PC's VLAN 10. What should be configured?

options.text: switchport access vlan 10 / switchport voice vlan 50
switchport mode trunk with native VLAN 50
Two separate cables, one for each device
options.note: The phone has a built-in switch.

options.text: switchport access vlan 50 / switchport voice vlan 10

explanation: The voice VLAN is communicated to the phone (usually via CDP or LLDP-MED); the phone tags voice traffic while the PC's traffic stays untagged.

scenario: Which DTP setting stops a port from negotiating a trunk?

options.note: Actively tries to form a trunk.
Forms a trunk if the other side asks.

explanation: Disabling DTP and setting access or trunk mode statically prevents switch spoofing attacks.

scenario: Which output shows which VLANs are allowed and active on each trunk?

options.note: Shows access port VLAN assignments, not trunks.

explanation: show interfaces trunk lists trunk ports, encapsulation, native VLAN, allowed VLANs and VLANs forwarding.

scenario: On a multilayer switch, which commands create a routed gateway for VLAN 20?

options.text: interface vlan 20 / switchport access vlan 20 / no shutdown

options.note: VLAN configuration mode doesn't take IP addresses.

explanation: SVIs provide inter-VLAN routing on layer 3 switches. ip routing must also be enabled for the switch to route between them.

scenario: Which command turns a switch port into a routed (layer 3) port?

options.text: switchport mode trunk on each member

explanation: no switchport converts the interface to a routed port that can take an IP address directly.

scenario: A router uses one interface for VLANs 10 and 20. Which configuration is correct for VLAN 10?

options.text: interface g0/0.10 / encapsulation dot1q 10 / ip address 10.10.0.1 255.255.255.0
interface g0/0 / switchport access vlan 10 / ip address 10.10.0.1 255.255.255.0
interface vlan 10 / ip address 10.10.0.1 255.255.255.0 on the router

explanation: Router-on-a-stick uses subinterfaces with 802.1Q encapsulation; the switch port facing the router must be a trunk.

scenario: Which LACP modes form an EtherChannel between two switches?

options.note: Mixing static on with LACP doesn't negotiate.

explanation: LACP active initiates negotiation, passive responds. At least one side must be active.

scenario: Which command bundles an interface into port-channel 1 using LACP active mode?
explanation: channel-group with mode active (or passive) uses LACP; desirable and auto use Cisco's PAgP; on forms a static channel.

scenario: An EtherChannel won't form. One member port is a trunk and the other is an access port. Why?

options.text: Member ports must have matching settings
EtherChannel only works on layer 3 routed ports

explanation: All member interfaces need consistent configuration, or they'll be suspended from the bundle.

scenario: A layer 3 EtherChannel is needed between two distribution switches. What must be configured on the port-channel interface?

options.text: no switchport and an IP address
switchport mode trunk on each member
A voice VLAN on the port-channel

explanation: A layer 3 EtherChannel is a routed port-channel; members are also configured with no switchport.

scenario: A new access point won't power on, and the switch log shows it was denied power. What should be checked?

options.text: The switch's PoE budget and the AP's power class
The OSPF router ID on the switch
The NAT pool on the edge router
The ACL applied to the WAN interface

explanation: show power inline displays available and used PoE. APs may need PoE+ or more power than the switch can supply.

scenario: A controller-based (lightweight) AP connects to an access switch. How is its switch port usually configured in local mode?

options.text: As an access port in the AP management VLAN
As a routed port with its own IP subnet
options.note: APs need layer 2 connectivity to their VLAN.

options.text: As a trunk carrying all VLANs, always
options.note: Typically for FlexConnect or autonomous APs.

options.text: Shut down until the controller is reachable
options.note: It needs the link to find the controller.

explanation: In local mode, client traffic is tunneled to the WLC with CAPWAP, so the AP needs only one access VLAN. FlexConnect or autonomous APs that switch traffic locally use trunks.

scenario: Which command shows the neighbor's IP address, platform and connected port?
explanation: CDP detail shows neighbor device ID, IP addresses, platform, software version and the local and remote interfaces.

scenario: A network includes switches from several vendors. Which protocol should be used to discover neighbors and validate cabling documentation?
explanation: LLDP (IEEE 802.1AB) is vendor-neutral. On Cisco IOS it's enabled globally with lldp run.

scenario: For security, CDP should be disabled on a port facing an ISP. Which interface command does this?

options.note: Disables CDP globally on the whole device.

explanation: no cdp enable disables CDP on one interface; no cdp run disables it on the whole device.

scenario: Which command gives a quick summary of every interface's IP address and up/down status?

options.note: Full config, not a status summary.

explanation: show ip interface brief is the fastest way to check addressing and interface status.

scenario: From router R1, a technician wants to ping a remote host using R1's loopback address as the source. What should they use?
explanation: Extended ping lets you set the source address or interface, repeat count, size and more. It's useful for testing routing for specific networks.

scenario: A traceroute from a router shows the first two hops, then asterisks on every following line. What does this suggest?

options.text: Traffic or ICMP is being dropped after hop two
The destination is reachable but slow to answer
The router's local outbound interface is down
DNS isn't configured, so hop names can't resolve

explanation: Asterisks mean no reply within the timeout. Check routing and ACLs on or after the last responding hop.

scenario: Which command lists the MAC addresses learned on each switch port?

options.text: show ip arp on the switch

explanation: The MAC address table maps MACs to ports and VLANs. It's useful to locate where a device is connected.

scenario: A switch log shows "%LINEPROTO-5-UPDOWN: Line protocol on Interface GigabitEthernet1/0/5, changed state to down" repeatedly. What does it suggest?

options.text: A flapping link, such as a bad cable
An STP root bridge change in the VLAN
A DHCP failure for the attached host
An ACL denying traffic on the port
options.note: ACLs don't change line protocol state.

explanation: Repeated up/down messages indicate an unstable link. Check cabling, transceivers, NIC power settings and the connected device.

scenario: Which show command displays the switch logs stored in its buffer?
explanation: show logging displays buffered syslog messages. Accurate time (NTP) makes logs much easier to correlate.

scenario: Which command makes switch SW1 the root bridge for VLAN 10, setting the priority low enough to win?
explanation: root primary sets priority to 24576, or lower if needed to beat the current root. root secondary sets 28672 for a backup root.

scenario: What is the default STP bridge priority on a Cisco switch for VLAN 1 with the extended system ID?

options.note: Base priority before adding the VLAN ID.
Highest possible priority, not the default.

explanation: The bridge priority is 32768 plus the VLAN ID (the extended system ID), so VLAN 1 gives 32769.

scenario: Which RSTP port role provides a backup path to the root bridge and stays discarding?
explanation: Alternate ports are backup paths to the root through another switch. Backup ports are backups to a segment through the same switch.

scenario: What are the RSTP port states?
explanation: RSTP combines blocking, listening and disabled into discarding.

scenario: Which feature lets an access port connected to a PC go straight to forwarding without waiting through STP states?
explanation: PortFast is for edge ports to hosts only. Pair it with BPDU Guard to protect against someone connecting a switch.

scenario: A user connects a small switch to a PortFast port, and the port goes err-disabled. Which feature caused this?

options.note: Puts the port in root-inconsistent state instead.

explanation: BPDU Guard err-disables an edge port that receives a BPDU, preventing unauthorized switches and loops.

scenario: A distribution switch should never accept a superior BPDU on ports facing the access layer, so no access switch becomes root. Which feature fits?

options.note: Shuts down on any BPDU; too aggressive for switch links.

explanation: Root Guard puts a port in a root-inconsistent (blocked) state if it receives a superior BPDU, and recovers when it stops.

scenario: A fiber link becomes unidirectional, and a blocking port stops receiving BPDUs and would start forwarding, creating a loop. Which feature prevents this?
explanation: Loop Guard puts a root or alternate port in a loop-inconsistent state when BPDUs stop arriving, instead of transitioning to forwarding.

scenario: In Rapid PVST+, how many STP instances run?

options.note: That's single-instance STP or MST with one instance.

explanation: Per-VLAN STP lets different VLANs use different root bridges and paths, balancing load across links.

scenario: Which port on a non-root switch becomes the root port?

options.text: The port with the lowest cost path to the root bridge
The port connected to the neighbor with the highest MAC address
The first port to come up
Any port that has PortFast enabled

explanation: Root port selection: lowest root path cost, then lowest neighbor bridge ID, then lowest neighbor port priority/ID.

scenario: A port is in err-disabled state after a security violation. How can it be recovered manually?

options.text: shutdown then no shutdown on the interface
clear mac address-table dynamic on the switch

explanation: Err-disabled ports stay down until manually re-enabled or errdisable recovery is configured.

scenario: Which command displays the status of all VLANs and their assigned access ports?
explanation: show vlan brief lists VLAN IDs, names, status and access ports. Trunk ports aren't listed there.

scenario: Hosts in VLAN 10 on two switches can't communicate. Both access ports are in VLAN 10, and the trunk is up. What should be checked next?

options.text: Whether VLAN 10 is allowed on the trunk
The OSPF area of the distribution switch
The NAT configuration on the edge router
The DNS server used by the hosts

explanation: If a VLAN isn't in the allowed list, or doesn't exist on one switch, its traffic won't cross the trunk. Check show interfaces trunk.

scenario: Which configuration is recommended for unused switch ports?

options.text: Shut them down and assign them to an unused VLAN
Configure them as trunks in case they're needed
Leave them in VLAN 1 and enabled

explanation: Disabling unused ports and placing them in a parking VLAN reduces the risk of unauthorized access.

scenario: A switch needs remote management. What must be configured?

options.text: An SVI with an IP address and a default gateway
A routed port with an IP address on every interface
A DHCP pool configured on the switch itself
A voice VLAN on the port-channel

explanation: A layer 2 switch is managed through an SVI IP address, with ip default-gateway for reaching other subnets.

scenario: Two switches are connected with three links, and Rapid PVST+ is running. How many links forward traffic for a given VLAN?

options.note: STP blocks redundant paths unless they're bundled.

explanation: STP allows one forwarding path per VLAN between two switches. Bundle the links in an EtherChannel to use all of them.

scenario: On a trunk, which VLAN's traffic is sent without an 802.1Q tag by default?

options.text: No VLAN; 802.1Q tags all traffic on a trunk
options.note: The native VLAN is untagged by default.

explanation: Changing the native VLAN to an unused VLAN and tagging it is a security best practice against VLAN hopping.

scenario: Which output confirms that port Gi1/0/2 is part of a working EtherChannel?
explanation: In show etherchannel summary, P means bundled in the port-channel, and s or I flags mean suspended or standalone.

scenario: Based on the routing table below, which next hop does R1 use for a packet to 10.2.5.9?

options.note: The default route is used only if nothing more specific matches.

explanation: The longest prefix match wins: 10.2.5.0/24 is more specific than 10.2.0.0/16, so the next hop is 10.1.1.3.
code:
R1# show ip route
Gateway of last resort is 203.0.113.1 to network 0.0.0.0

S*    0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 203.0.113.1
      10.0.0.0/8 is variably subnetted, 4 subnets, 3 masks
C        10.1.1.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
L        10.1.1.1/32 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
O        10.2.0.0/16 [110/2] via 10.1.1.2, 00:12:44, GigabitEthernet0/0
O        10.2.5.0/24 [110/3] via 10.1.1.3, 00:12:44, GigabitEthernet0/0

scenario: Based on the routing table below, where does R1 send a packet for 172.16.4.4?

options.text: It's dropped because there's no specific route

explanation: S* marks a static default route (0.0.0.0/0), the gateway of last resort for destinations with no more specific match.
code:
R1# show ip route
Gateway of last resort is 203.0.113.1 to network 0.0.0.0

S*    0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 203.0.113.1
      10.0.0.0/8 is variably subnetted, 4 subnets, 3 masks
C        10.1.1.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
L        10.1.1.1/32 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
O        10.2.0.0/16 [110/2] via 10.1.1.2, 00:12:44, GigabitEthernet0/0
O        10.2.5.0/24 [110/3] via 10.1.1.3, 00:12:44, GigabitEthernet0/0

scenario: In the routing table below, what do the values in [110/2] mean?

options.text: OSPF area 110 and a hop count of 2
OSPF process ID 110 and an interface cost of 2
options.note: AD is first, not process ID.

explanation: The bracket shows [administrative distance/metric]. OSPF's default AD is 110, and the metric is the OSPF cost.
code:
R1# show ip route
Gateway of last resort is 203.0.113.1 to network 0.0.0.0

S*    0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 203.0.113.1
      10.0.0.0/8 is variably subnetted, 4 subnets, 3 masks
C        10.1.1.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
L        10.1.1.1/32 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
O        10.2.0.0/16 [110/2] via 10.1.1.2, 00:12:44, GigabitEthernet0/0
O        10.2.5.0/24 [110/3] via 10.1.1.3, 00:12:44, GigabitEthernet0/0

scenario: What does the code "L" mean in an IOS routing table?

options.text: A /32 route for the router's own interface IP
A route learned from an OSPF router LSA
A route leaked into the table from another VRF
A network on a loopback interface
options.note: Loopback networks show as C plus L.

explanation: IOS adds an L (local) host route for each interface IP address, alongside the C (connected) network route.

scenario: A router learns 10.5.0.0/24 from EIGRP (AD 90) and from OSPF (AD 110). Which route is installed?
explanation: When prefix lengths match, the lowest administrative distance wins. Metrics are only compared within the same protocol.

scenario: Which administrative distance values are correct for Cisco IOS?

options.text: All route sources share an AD of 1 by default

explanation: Other common values: eBGP 20, RIP 120, external EIGRP 170, iBGP 200. An AD of 255 means the route is never used.

scenario: Which command creates a static default route via next hop 198.51.100.1?
explanation: The syntax is ip route destination mask next-hop (or exit interface).

scenario: A backup static route should be used only if the OSPF-learned route to 10.9.0.0/16 disappears. How is it configured?

options.note: Keeps the route installed even if the interface is down; doesn't make it a backup.

explanation: A floating static route has an administrative distance higher than the primary route's, so it's installed only when the primary disappears.

scenario: Which static route matches only the single host 10.4.4.10?

options.note: Mask 0.0.0.0 would make this a default route.

explanation: A host route uses a /32 mask (255.255.255.255).

scenario: Which command creates an IPv6 static default route via next hop 2001:db8:ffff::1?
explanation: IPv6 static routes use ipv6 route prefix/length next-hop. ipv6 unicast-routing must be enabled.

scenario: An IPv6 static route uses a link-local next hop such as FE80::2. What else must the command include?

options.text: The OSPF area of the distribution switch

explanation: Link-local addresses are only unique on a link, so you specify the interface: ipv6 route 2001:db8:5::/64 g0/1 fe80::2.

scenario: R1 has a static route to 10.20.0.0/16 via 10.1.1.2, but pings to 10.20.1.1 fail. R1 can ping 10.1.1.2. What is a likely cause?

options.text: The remote network has no route back to R1's network
R1's static route syntax is invalid
R1 needs a default route to reach any remote network
The ping uses UDP, which static routes don't forward

explanation: Routing must work in both directions. Check the return path on the remote router as well as routing tables along the path.

scenario: How does OSPF choose its router ID if none is configured manually?

options.text: Highest loopback IPv4 address, else highest active interface IPv4
The lowest IPv4 address on any active interface, including loopbacks
The MAC address of the first interface that came up
A random 32-bit number generated at startup

explanation: Configure router-id manually for predictability. Changes take effect after clearing the OSPF process (clear ip ospf process).

scenario: Two OSPF routers on the same subnet are stuck and never become neighbors. One has hello/dead timers of 10/40, the other 5/20. What is the problem?

options.text: Hello and dead timers must match
Router IDs must match on both routers
options.note: Router IDs must be unique, not matching.

options.text: Interface priorities must match on the subnet

options.note: OSPF process IDs are locally significant.

explanation: Neighbors must agree on area ID, subnet, hello/dead timers, authentication and stub flags. MTU mismatches stall adjacency in ExStart/Exchange.

scenario: Two OSPF neighbors are stuck in the ExStart/Exchange state. Which mismatch is most likely?
explanation: MTU mismatches prevent database description exchange. Match MTUs, or use ip ospf mtu-ignore as a workaround.

scenario: Which commands enable OSPF area 0 on GigabitEthernet0/1 using interface configuration?

options.note: network statements take addresses and wildcards.

explanation: OSPF can be enabled per interface (ip ospf process-id area area-id) or with network address wildcard area statements under router ospf.

scenario: Which network statement enables OSPF area 0 on all interfaces in 10.1.0.0/16?

options.note: OSPF network statements use wildcard masks.
IOS doesn't accept prefix notation here.

explanation: OSPF network statements use wildcard masks to select interfaces.

scenario: An OSPF router shouldn't send hello packets out its LAN interface facing users, but the LAN should still be advertised. What should be configured?

options.text: no network statement for the LAN

explanation: Passive interfaces are advertised in OSPF but don't form adjacencies, which improves security and reduces overhead.

scenario: On a broadcast segment, which router becomes the OSPF DR?

options.text: Highest interface priority, then highest router ID
Lowest interface priority, then lowest router ID
The router with the most neighbors
Always the first router to boot
options.note: It can win only because election isn't preemptive.

explanation: Default priority is 1. Priority 0 means the router can't become DR or BDR. The election isn't preemptive: a better router added later doesn't take over until the DR fails.

scenario: Which OSPF interface priority prevents a router from ever becoming DR or BDR?
explanation: Set ip ospf priority 0 on routers that shouldn't take part in DR election.

scenario: Two routers connect over a point-to-point Ethernet link and run OSPF. How can DR/BDR election and its delay be avoided?

options.text: ip ospf network point-to-point on both interfaces
ip ospf priority 255 on both interfaces
Put each interface in a different OSPF area
Disable hello packets on the link

explanation: OSPF point-to-point network type doesn't elect a DR or BDR, which speeds up adjacency on two-router links.

scenario: On a broadcast segment with a DR and BDR, which state do two DROTHER routers reach with each other?

options.note: DROTHERs reach Full only with the DR and BDR.

explanation: DROTHERs stay in 2-Way with each other, which is normal. They form Full adjacencies with the DR and BDR.

scenario: OSPF calculates the same cost of 1 for 1 Gbps and 10 Gbps links. Why?

options.text: The default reference bandwidth is 100 Mbps
OSPF uses hop count rather than bandwidth
OSPF ignores bandwidth on Ethernet links
The links are in different areas

explanation: Cost = reference bandwidth / interface bandwidth, with a minimum of 1. Raise it with auto-cost reference-bandwidth (consistently on all routers).

scenario: Which command makes an OSPF router advertise its default route to other OSPF routers?
explanation: default-information originate advertises a default route if the router has one (or always, with the always keyword).

scenario: Which multicast address do all OSPFv2 routers listen to for hello packets?
explanation: 224.0.0.5 reaches all OSPF routers; 224.0.0.6 reaches the DR and BDR. OSPFv3 uses FF02::5 and FF02::6.

scenario: Which command verifies OSPF neighbors and their states?
explanation: show ip ospf neighbor lists neighbor IDs, priorities, states (such as FULL/DR) and interfaces.

scenario: How is OSPFv3 enabled for IPv6 on an interface?
explanation: OSPFv3 is configured per interface. It uses link-local addresses for neighbor communication and still needs a 32-bit router ID.

scenario: What must be true for OSPFv3 to start if a router has no IPv4 addresses at all?

options.text: A router ID must be configured manually
An IPv6 global address is used as the router ID
OSPFv3 doesn't need a router ID
The router must also run OSPFv2

explanation: OSPFv3 router IDs are 32-bit numbers. Without IPv4 addresses, set router-id manually.

scenario: In OSPF, which state indicates that two routers have fully synchronized their link-state databases?
explanation: Neighbor states: Down, Init, 2-Way, ExStart, Exchange, Loading, Full.

scenario: show standby brief on R2 shows State "Standby" and Active router 10.1.1.2. What does this mean?

options.text: R2 is the backup and takes over on failure
R2 is forwarding traffic for the virtual IP
HSRP isn't working and no router is forwarding
R2 is the VRRP master for the group

explanation: In HSRP, the active router forwards traffic for the virtual IP and MAC; the standby router monitors and takes over on failure.

scenario: Which statement is true about HSRP preemption on Cisco routers?

options.text: It's off by default and must be enabled with standby preempt
It's always on by default and can't be disabled
It only applies to VRRP, not to HSRP
It requires OSPF to track the uplink

explanation: HSRP's default priority is 100 and preemption is off. VRRP enables preemption by default.

scenario: Which first hop redundancy protocol is an open standard?
explanation: VRRP is an IETF standard. Its roles are master and backup; HSRP uses active and standby.

scenario: What do end hosts use as their default gateway when an FHRP is configured?

options.text: The virtual IP address shared by the routers
The active router's physical interface IP
The standby router's physical interface IP

explanation: Hosts use the virtual IP, which maps to a virtual MAC, so failover is transparent to them.

scenario: Two routers both show HSRP state "Active" for the same group. What is a likely cause?

options.text: The virtual IP is in the same subnet

explanation: If routers can't hear each other's hellos, each assumes it's active. Check layer 2 connectivity, VLANs and group numbers.

scenario: Which command increases R1's HSRP priority so it can become active (with preemption)?
explanation: Higher priority wins the active role. With preemption, R1 takes over even if another router is already active.

scenario: R1's routing table shows two equal-cost OSPF routes to the same network via different next hops. What does R1 do?

options.text: Uses only the first route learned and keeps the other as backup
Drops traffic because the routes are ambiguous
Uses the path with the lower router ID

explanation: OSPF supports equal-cost multipath (ECMP), with up to four paths by default on IOS (configurable with maximum-paths).

scenario: Which command creates a local user with an encrypted (hashed) password on IOS?

options.note: Stored with weak or no encryption.
Sets the enable password, not a user.
A line password, not a user.

explanation: secret stores a strong hash. Combine local users with login local on VTY lines and SSH.

scenario: Network admins should authenticate to routers using a TACACS+ server, falling back to local accounts if the server is unreachable. Which command does this?

options.text: aaa authentication login default group tacacs+ local
aaa authentication login default local group tacacs+
login tacacs+ local on the VTY lines

explanation: aaa new-model must be enabled first. Methods are tried in order; local is used only if the server doesn't respond.

scenario: Which is a key advantage of TACACS+ over RADIUS for device administration?

options.text: It encrypts the full payload and authorizes per command
It uses UDP 1812 for faster authentication
It's an open IEEE standard used by all vendors

explanation: TACACS+ separates authentication, authorization and accounting. RADIUS (UDP 1812/1813) combines authentication and authorization and encrypts only the password.

scenario: Which steps are required to enable SSH on a Cisco router?

options.text: Hostname, domain name, RSA keys, and transport input ssh
Enable Telnet and set a VTY password
Configure an ACL that permits TCP 22 only
Enable ip http server and set a password

explanation: Typical steps: hostname, ip domain-name, crypto key generate rsa (2048+ bits), ip ssh version 2, local users or AAA, and transport input ssh with login local on VTY lines.

scenario: Which command restricts SSH access to the router to the management subnet using ACL 10?
explanation: access-class applies an ACL to VTY lines to control which source addresses can open management sessions.

scenario: Which protocol should be used to copy an IOS image to a router securely?
explanation: SCP and SFTP run over SSH. On IOS, the SCP server is enabled with ip scp server enable.

scenario: Which command backs up the running configuration to an SCP server?
explanation: IOS copy commands accept URL-style destinations such as scp://, sftp:// and tftp://.

scenario: Which command configures PAT so inside hosts in ACL 1 share the address of interface G0/1?

options.text: ip nat inside source list 1 interface g0/1 overload
ip nat outside source list 1 interface g0/1
ip nat inside source static 10.0.0.0 g0/1
ip nat pool overload g0/1 netmask 255.255.255.0

explanation: The overload keyword enables PAT. Interfaces also need ip nat inside and ip nat outside.

scenario: A web server at 10.1.1.10 must be reachable from the internet at 203.0.113.10. Which command creates this mapping?

options.text: ip nat inside source list 1 pool WEB

explanation: Static NAT creates a permanent one-to-one mapping, allowing inbound connections to the inside server.

scenario: In Cisco NAT terminology, what is the "inside global" address?

options.text: The public address representing an inside host
The private address assigned to the inside host
The address of the remote server as seen outside
The router's loopback address used for NAT

explanation: Inside local = private address on the inside. Inside global = translated public address. Outside global = the external host's real address.

scenario: Users can't reach the internet. show ip nat translations shows no entries. What should be checked first?

options.text: The ip nat inside/outside interfaces and the NAT ACL
The OSPF priority on the internet-facing interface
The STP root bridge for the user VLANs
The DHCP excluded addresses on the LAN pool

explanation: Common NAT faults: missing or swapped inside/outside interface statements, an ACL that doesn't match the inside network, or no route to the internet.

scenario: Users can reach a web server by IP address but not by its name, www.example.com. Which DNS record should be checked first?

options.text: The NS record of an unrelated domain

explanation: A records map names to IPv4 addresses and AAAA records map names to IPv6 addresses. A missing or wrong record breaks name-based access.

scenario: Email to @example.com is bouncing, but the website works. Which DNS record is most likely wrong?
explanation: MX records direct mail to the domain's mail servers. Check that they point to a hostname that has a valid A or AAAA record.

scenario: shop.example.com should point to the same server as www.example.com, and follow it if its address changes. Which record should be used?

options.text: A with a copy of the IP address
options.note: Must be updated manually if the IP changes.

explanation: A CNAME is an alias to another name, so it follows the target's address automatically.

scenario: Logs show IP addresses instead of hostnames because reverse lookups fail. Which record type is missing?
explanation: PTR records in the reverse zone (in-addr.arpa or ip6.arpa) map IP addresses back to names.

scenario: Which DNS record identifies the authoritative name servers for a zone?
explanation: NS records delegate a zone to its authoritative servers. Wrong NS records at the registrar break resolution for the whole domain.

scenario: Which command makes a Cisco router resolve hostnames using DNS server 8.8.8.8?

options.note: Enables the router as a DNS server.

explanation: ip name-server configures DNS servers for the router's own lookups. dns-server inside a DHCP pool hands addresses to clients.

scenario: Two branch routers need an always-on encrypted tunnel between their LANs over the internet. Which VPN type fits?

options.text: A GRE tunnel without IPsec protection
SSL clientless portal for each branch

explanation: Site-to-site VPNs connect networks via gateways. Remote-access VPNs connect individual users with a client.

scenario: Which IPsec protocol provides encryption?
explanation: ESP provides confidentiality, integrity and authentication. IKE (UDP 500, or 4500 with NAT traversal) builds the security associations.

scenario: What is the difference between IPsec tunnel mode and transport mode?

options.text: Tunnel mode protects the whole original packet; transport mode protects only the payload
Transport mode is used between VPN gateways; tunnel mode is host-to-host
Tunnel mode only adds a header and doesn't encrypt anything
They're the same, but tunnel mode uses AH

explanation: Site-to-site VPNs typically use tunnel mode. Transport mode is used host-to-host or with GRE over IPsec.

scenario: Which ACL type filters only on source IP address?

options.note: Can match protocol, source, destination and ports.

explanation: Standard ACLs match source addresses only. Place them as close to the destination as possible.

scenario: Where should an extended ACL generally be placed?

options.text: As close to the source as possible
As close to the destination as possible
options.note: That's the guidance for standard ACLs.

options.text: Only on VTY lines, using access-class

explanation: Extended ACLs are specific enough to drop unwanted traffic early, saving bandwidth along the path.

scenario: Which ACL entry permits HTTPS from any host to web server 10.1.1.10?

options.text: access-list 110 permit tcp any host 10.1.1.10 eq 443
access-list 110 permit udp any host 10.1.1.10 eq 443
options.note: HTTPS uses TCP (HTTP/3 uses UDP, but classic HTTPS is TCP).

options.text: access-list 110 permit tcp host 10.1.1.10 any eq 443

explanation: Extended ACL syntax: permit/deny, protocol, source, destination, then port operators such as eq.

scenario: An ACL contains only access-list 101 deny tcp any any eq 23 and is applied inbound. What happens to web traffic?

options.text: It's denied by the implicit deny at the end
It's permitted because only Telnet is denied

explanation: Every ACL ends with an implicit deny any. Add permit ip any any (or specific permits) after the deny lines.

scenario: Which wildcard mask in an ACL matches the subnet 10.10.16.0/20?

options.note: Not a valid contiguous wildcard for a /20.

scenario: Which command applies named ACL BLOCK-GUEST to traffic entering G0/2?
explanation: ip access-group name-or-number in|out applies an ACL to an interface. Each interface supports one ACL per direction per protocol.

scenario: Which keyword in an ACL matches a single host?
Which feature stops rogue DHCP servers by allowing DHCP server messages only on trusted ports?
explanation: Mark uplinks toward legitimate DHCP servers as trusted; access ports stay untrusted. Snooping also builds a binding table used by DAI.

scenario: Which feature uses the DHCP snooping binding table to block forged ARP replies?
explanation: DAI validates ARP packets on untrusted ports against IP-to-MAC bindings, preventing ARP poisoning.

scenario: Port security is configured with maximum 1 and the default violation mode. What happens when a second MAC address appears?

options.text: Traffic from the new MAC is dropped silently and nothing is logged
Traffic is dropped and a counter increments, but the port stays up

explanation: Violation modes: shutdown (default), restrict (drop and log) and protect (drop silently).

scenario: Which port security option dynamically learns MAC addresses and saves them to the running configuration?
explanation: Sticky MAC addresses are learned and added to the running config; save the config to keep them after a reload.

scenario: A broadcast storm should be automatically limited on access ports. Which feature fits?
explanation: Storm control drops (or shuts the port) when broadcast, multicast or unknown unicast traffic exceeds a threshold.

scenario: Which feature blocks IPv6 router advertisements from unauthorized devices on access ports?
explanation: Rogue RAs can redirect IPv6 traffic. RA Guard allows RAs only from authorized router ports.

scenario: With DHCP snooping enabled, legitimate clients stop getting addresses. The DHCP server is reached through the uplink. What is the likely fix?

options.text: Trust the uplink toward the DHCP server
Disable PortFast on the client access ports
Change the native VLAN on the uplink
Enable BPDU Guard on the uplink

explanation: All ports are untrusted by default, so server replies on the uplink are dropped until it's trusted (ip dhcp snooping trust).

scenario: Which is the most secure way to manage network devices remotely?

options.text: SSH with AAA from a restricted management subnet
HTTP web interface with local accounts
SNMPv1 read-write with a private community

explanation: Use encrypted protocols (SSH, HTTPS, SNMPv3), centralized AAA, and restrict management access by source address.

scenario: Which ACL statement number range identifies an extended IPv4 ACL?

options.note: Ethernet type codes (legacy), not extended IP.

explanation: Numbered extended IPv4 ACLs use 100–199 and 2000–2699. Named ACLs are easier to read and edit.

scenario: What distinguishes agentic AI from a basic generative AI chatbot in network operations?

options.text: It can plan steps and use tools to take actions toward a goal
It only generates text answers to the questions it's asked
It requires no permissions, guardrails or oversight
It replaces routing protocols with learned paths

explanation: Agentic AI systems pursue goals by calling tools and APIs. In networking they need least-privilege access, approval steps for changes and human review.

scenario: An engineer asks a public generative AI tool to troubleshoot a config. What should they do with the configuration first?

options.text: Remove or mask passwords, keys and other sensitive data
Paste it exactly as is so the AI has full context
Encrypt it first so the AI provider can't read it
Convert it to a screenshot so the text isn't stored

explanation: Consider data classification before prompting. Don't share confidential data with tools that aren't approved for it.

scenario: An engineer wants an AI assistant to produce an ACL. Which prompt is most likely to get a useful result?

options.text: As a Cisco engineer, write an IOS extended ACL permitting HTTPS from 10.1.0.0/16 to 10.9.9.10, denying all else. Output only commands.
Make an ACL for my network that blocks the bad traffic.
Fix my network, it's slow and some users can't connect to the server.
Write something about network security and ACLs for our company.

explanation: Effective prompts give a persona, clear instructions, context and the desired output format, while respecting data classification.

scenario: An AI assistant recommends a configuration change for a production router. What should happen before it's applied?

options.text: An engineer validates and tests it, then it goes through change control
Apply it immediately, because AI recommendations are always correct
Apply it to all routers at once during business hours
Ignore it entirely, because AI output can't be used in production
options.note: Recommendations can be useful after review.

explanation: AI output must be evaluated by people. Validate recommendations, test them, and follow change management.

scenario: Which is an appropriate task for predictive AI in network operations?

options.text: Forecasting when link utilization will run out
Replacing STP with a learned loop-free topology
Assigning MAC addresses to new interfaces
Creating new IP protocols for the WAN

explanation: Predictive AI and machine learning analyze telemetry to forecast trends and detect anomalies. Generative AI produces text, code and summaries.

scenario: A company manages hundreds of switches through a central dashboard hosted by the vendor, accessible from anywhere. Which management approach is this?
explanation: Cloud-managed platforms (such as Meraki) provide centralized configuration and monitoring without on-premises controllers.

scenario: A central controller pushes policies to switches and routers, separating the control plane from the devices. Which approach is this?

options.note: Controllers may be on premises or in the cloud.

explanation: In controller-based networks, a controller (such as Catalyst Center) uses northbound APIs to apps and southbound APIs to devices.

scenario: What is a key benefit of infrastructure as code for network configuration?

options.text: Configurations are version-controlled, reviewable and repeatable
It removes the need for testing changes before deployment
It only works with one vendor's devices

explanation: IaC tools (such as Ansible or Terraform) define desired state in files stored in source control, reducing configuration drift and manual errors.

scenario: Which statement about Ansible is correct?

options.text: It's agentless and uses YAML playbooks, often over SSH
It requires an agent installed on every router
It uses XML templates and requires NETCONF on every device
It replaces SNMP monitoring and syslog

explanation: Ansible uses an inventory of devices and playbooks of tasks, and has modules for running commands on network devices (for example ios_command).

scenario: Which file in an Ansible project lists the devices to be managed?
explanation: The inventory lists hosts and groups. Playbooks describe the tasks to run against them.

scenario: What is the role of an SNMP agent?

options.text: It runs on the managed device and answers the manager
It's the central monitoring server that polls devices
It collects and forwards syslog messages to the server
It encrypts all management traffic between devices

explanation: SNMP managers poll agents (UDP 161) for MIB data, and agents send traps or informs (UDP 162) for events.

scenario: Which SNMP version should be used for secure monitoring?

options.text: SNMPv2c with a long community string

explanation: SNMPv3 authPriv provides authentication and encryption.

scenario: What is the difference between an SNMP trap and an inform?

options.text: Informs are acknowledged by the manager; traps aren't
A trap is sent by the manager to request data
Informs use TCP 22, while traps use UDP 162
There's no difference other than the name

explanation: Informs are more reliable because the agent resends them if they aren't acknowledged.

scenario: What do the parts of the syslog message %LINK-3-UPDOWN mean?
explanation: Cisco syslog format is %FACILITY-SEVERITY-MNEMONIC: description.

scenario: Which syslog severity level corresponds to warnings?
explanation: Levels: 0 emergencies, 1 alerts, 2 critical, 3 errors, 4 warnings, 5 notifications, 6 informational, 7 debugging.

scenario: The command logging trap 4 is configured. Which messages are sent to the syslog server?

options.note: It includes all more severe levels.

options.text: All messages from level 0 through level 7

explanation: A logging level sends that level and all more severe (lower-numbered) messages.

scenario: Why should network devices synchronize time with NTP before sending logs to a syslog server?

options.text: So timestamps are accurate and events can be correlated
NTP encrypts the syslog messages in transit
Syslog messages won't be sent at all without NTP
options.note: It works, but timestamps may be wrong.

options.text: NTP reduces the bandwidth used by syslog

explanation: Consistent timestamps (with service timestamps log datetime) are essential for troubleshooting and security investigations.

scenario: Which syslog facility appears in the message %SEC-6-IPACCESSLOGP?
explanation: SEC is the facility, 6 is informational severity, and IPACCESSLOGP indicates an ACL log entry.

scenario: A branch needs 50 usable host addresses in one subnet with as little waste as possible. Which prefix length should be used?
explanation: A /26 gives 64 addresses (62 usable), the smallest block that fits 50 hosts.

scenario: Which address is a valid host in the subnet 192.168.20.64/27?
explanation: 192.168.20.64/27 spans .64–.95. Usable hosts are .65 through .94.

scenario: Two buildings 10 km apart must be connected with a 10 Gbps fiber link. Which fiber type fits?

options.text: Multimode OM3 fiber with short-reach optics
options.note: Multimode reaches only a few hundred meters at 10 Gbps.

options.text: Multimode OM4 fiber with SR optics
options.note: Still limited to a few hundred meters.

explanation: Single-mode fiber uses a small core and lasers for long distances (10GBASE-LR reaches 10 km). Multimode suits shorter runs inside buildings.

scenario: What is the compressed form of 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:ff00:0042:8329?
explanation: Remove leading zeros in each group and replace one run of all-zero groups with ::.

scenario: A host needs to resolve the MAC address of its IPv6 default gateway. Which mechanism does it use?
explanation: IPv6 uses Neighbor Discovery (ICMPv6 types 135/136) instead of ARP. Routers are found with RS/RA messages.

scenario: Which wireless architecture uses lightweight APs that tunnel client traffic to a WLC with CAPWAP?
explanation: Lightweight APs handle real-time functions, while the WLC handles management. CAPWAP uses UDP 5246 (control) and 5247 (data).

scenario: Which IPv6 address type is automatically created on every IPv6-enabled interface and used for neighbor discovery?
explanation: Every IPv6 interface has a link-local address. Routing protocols such as OSPFv3 use link-local addresses as next hops.

scenario: Hosts should build their own global IPv6 addresses from the prefix in router advertisements, without a DHCPv6 server. What is this called?
explanation: With SLAAC, hosts combine the RA prefix with a self-generated interface ID (EUI-64 or random). Stateless DHCPv6 can add options like DNS servers.

scenario: A switch receives a frame for a destination MAC that isn't in its MAC address table. What does it do?

options.text: Floods it out all other ports in the VLAN
Drops the frame and logs an error
Sends it to the default gateway
Sends it only out the trunk ports

explanation: Unknown unicast frames are flooded. The switch learns source MAC addresses from incoming frames.

scenario: How long does a Cisco switch keep a dynamically learned MAC address by default if no traffic is seen?

options.note: That's the default ARP timeout on routers.

explanation: The default MAC address aging time is 300 seconds (5 minutes).

scenario: Which DTP mode combination results in a trunk?
explanation: Best practice is to hard-code trunks with switchport mode trunk and disable DTP using switchport nonegotiate.

scenario: A switch port is err-disabled, and the log shows %PORT_SECURITY-2-PSECURE_VIOLATION. What happened?

options.text: A port security violation, such as too many MAC addresses
A BPDU was received on a PortFast edge port
options.note: That logs a BPDU Guard message.

options.text: The link flapped too many times in a short period
A duplex mismatch was detected by CDP
options.note: CDP logs a duplex mismatch warning only.

explanation: In the default shutdown mode, a port security violation err-disables the port. Fix the cause, then shut/no shut the port or configure errdisable recovery.

scenario: Which command changes the native VLAN on a trunk to unused VLAN 999?
explanation: Use an unused native VLAN, set it the same on both ends, and avoid carrying user traffic in it to reduce VLAN-hopping risk.

scenario: A branch AP is managed by a WLC at headquarters, but branch client traffic should be switched locally instead of tunneled to the WLC. Which AP mode fits?

options.note: Traffic is tunneled to the WLC.

explanation: FlexConnect APs can switch client traffic locally at a branch while still being managed by a remote WLC.

scenario: A WLAN must map to VLAN 30 on a WLC. What must exist on the WLC to support this?

options.text: A dynamic interface tied to VLAN 30
An SVI for VLAN 30 on each AP
options.note: APs don't have SVIs for WLANs.

options.text: A routed port with an IP in VLAN 30

explanation: WLC dynamic interfaces map WLANs to VLANs. The WLC's distribution port is typically an 802.1Q trunk.

scenario: Which protocol keeps an EtherChannel working when both ends must be standards-based and vendor-neutral?
explanation: LACP uses active/passive modes. PAgP uses desirable/auto. Static mode on doesn't negotiate.
192.168.1.200 is in .128–.255, so the /25 is the longest matching prefix.

scenario: Which command shows OSPF interface details such as cost, state, DR and timers?
explanation: show ip ospf interface (or interface brief) shows area, cost, network type, DR/BDR and hello/dead timers.

scenario: Which command sets the OSPF cost on interface G0/1 to 50?

options.note: Changes bandwidth, which indirectly affects cost.
Changes reference bandwidth for all interfaces.

explanation: ip ospf cost overrides the calculated cost on an interface.

scenario: A router has an OSPF route to 10.30.0.0/24 and a static route to the same prefix with the default AD. Which is installed?

options.note: OSPF's AD (110) is higher than static (1).

explanation: Static routes have AD 1 by default and are preferred over OSPF (110) for the same prefix length.

scenario: Which NTP feature makes sure a router only accepts time from trusted servers?
